text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesay.
- President Tudjman to return to Croatia from Washington on Friday or Saturday at the latest.
- Does the resignation of the Bosnain Federation defence minister Vladimir Soljic have anything to do with the way positions in the Bosnian Federation are distributed?
- War invalids to be awarded 15, 500 flats by the year 2001.
- The project of mass privatisation worth 27.1 million kuna has been included in the 1997 budget. It could commence at the beginning of 1997.
- BEMEX touroperator owned by national oil firm INA to be sold.
- The 1997 budget proposal is ignoring VAT.
- Monopoly and secret deals to come under scrutiny, says Desa Mlikotin-Tomic, head of the agency for the protection of market competition.
- Is the electrical manufacturer Koncar to float its shares abroad?
- Local Serb authorities in the last rebel enclave of Eastern Slavonia are issuing false residents' papers to immigrants from Serbia to enable them to stay in the region.
- Croatia can hope to catch up with Europe only with 10 percent production rate increase.

- EBRD's purchase of shares in Varazdinska Banka lifted its price by 122 percent last month. Shipping companies including Atlantska Plovidba, Tankerska Plovidba and Jadroplov were also among the best buys.
- Commentary: Instead of being a reliable indicator, our statistics is merely a manipulation in government's day-to-day interests, Josip Valter said. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
